mbta_reduced_list.overlap_note: this operator's two goods carry one value each, so the pairs inside a list are one fact per list, not one per pair (D22). the three federally named classes at this operator are also counted in transit_federal_three; the reduced list is not that partition, since it lists disability and Medicare as a single entry
mbta_reduced_list.partition: the four entries under the heading Riders Eligible for Reduced Fares on the operator's own page
mbta_reduced_list.source: mbta.com/fares/reduced and mbta.com/fares, both retrieved 2026-09-07 by browser
mbta_reduced_list.why: the heading is Riders Eligible for Reduced Fares, which does not fix WHICH reduced fare. another operator prints three different reduced columns under the same idea, so several values are available under this label

rtd_discount_four.line: the four classes this operator's own footnote names for one discount column
rtd_discount_four.merge_declared_note: this operator both names the partition and puts it in one column, and presents the consolidation as policy. that does not weaken the reading, since four verified classes still carry one price, but it is not a merge discovered across independent tables the way the statute row is

near_refutation.reading: the income line separates from the disability line there, 450 against 225. Q0 was set before this page was read and door-to-door is not the same commodity, so this does not enter the row, and it is the closest thing to a refutation the corpus holds
near_refutation.where: the operator's paratransit service, which fails Q0

rtd_discount_four.partition: the four classes named in one sentence of the footnote to the Standard and Discount Fares table, less the airport day pass row whose discount cell reads no additional charge rather than a price
rtd_discount_four.why: the heading is Discount Fares, which does not fix WHICH discount; the same page prices a different discount structure on its paratransit service and prices youth at zero

sg_emergency_rule.cells_are_not_figures: the announcement says emergency department fees will not discriminate between nationality or citizenship. what was read is that the three cells are equal; their shared level is not on that page. the cells carry a marker rather than a number, and this row is excluded from the exact-integer premise for that reason
sg_emergency_rule.line: the same three residency statuses, in the one place the same document forbids the distinction
sg_emergency_rule.partition: the same three statuses named by the same announcement
sg_emergency_rule.source: Singapore Ministry of Health published announcement on the revision of hospital subsidy for foreigners, read 2026-09-08. subsidy percentages by ward class and residency status, at their announcement date and not claimed current
sg_emergency_rule.the_object: a zero of a kind not otherwise on this board. it is not a merge the seller chose, and not one its credentials forced. a published rule bans the line in this one context while the same document draws it in five others
sg_emergency_rule.why: the labels name residency, not a number, and the same document prints five rows in which they take different values

sg_subsidy_residency.line: the three residency statuses the health ministry's own subsidy table prints
sg_subsidy_residency.partition: the columns of the published subsidy table, Singapore citizen, permanent resident and foreigner
sg_subsidy_residency.source: Singapore Ministry of Health published announcement on the revision of hospital subsidy for foreigners, read 2026-09-08. subsidy percentages by ward class and residency status, at their announcement date and not claimed current
sg_subsidy_residency.the_object: fifteen pairs, fifteen separations, and the gap between citizen and permanent resident is five points in every row but the first, where it is ten. what is published is a percentage off a common bill, which is why B54 reads this carrier's second question as failing while this row reads its class values
sg_subsidy_residency.why: the table prints three different figures under these headings in every one of its rows

state_park_residence.line: resident against non-resident, the two columns two state park systems print
state_park_residence.partition: the column headers of the published camping fee schedules, RESIDENT and NON-RESIDENT
state_park_residence.source: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands published fee schedule and Rhode Island State Parks published camping policies, both read 2026-09-08
state_park_residence.the_object: sixteen sites, sixteen separations, no site where the two columns carry the same figure. the ratio is not constant either: Maine runs from 1.40 to 1.67 and Rhode Island from 1.50 to 2.00, so this is not one multiplier applied to a base, which is what D30's third clause would make a single price
state_park_residence.why: the headers name who, and one of the two systems states the check and its consequence, so the sorting cost is paid

student_vs_senior.partition: two entries both operators list separately on their own reduced-fare pages, each with its own credential
student_vs_senior.source: the two operators' own fare pages, recomputed from the cells in B56
student_vs_senior.why: one of the two operators prices them apart, which settles it

transit_federal_three.line: the three lines the federal condition names
transit_federal_three.partition: the three classes named in 49 U.S.C. 5307(c)(1)(D), which is one list in one sentence of the statute
transit_federal_three.source: 49 U.S.C. 5307(c)(1)(D) and the operators' own fare pages, recomputed from the cells in B56
transit_federal_three.why: the statute caps the fare at half the peak fare and does not require the three to pay the same as each other, so three different values are fully available under this label

virginia_residency.partition: resident against non-resident, the two columns the fee schedule itself is written in

same_value_contexts: fish in designated stocked trout waters

virginia_residency.source: 4 Va. Admin. Code 15-20-65, recomputed from the cells in B55
